blocks.markdown: An example note made while reading the guide. Click a **memo card** to jump to that sentence in the PDF, and drag a block by its left handle to reorder it. Follow the “Try it” boxes in the guide and add memos of your own.

blocks.quote: A Vault is a plain folder, so you can copy or back it up with your file manager.
blocks.note: Copying the whole Vault folder is a backup. App records live in `.iwae`.

blocks.quote: Drag a tab to the edge of a pane and a new pane is created on that side.
blocks.note: Tabs reorder, move between panes, split at an edge, or detach into a window, all by dragging. Drag a detached window's tab back onto a tab bar to reattach it.

blocks.quote: A highlighted sentence is linked to its memo card by a thin line.
blocks.note: The line has the highlight's color. With several panes the note bar stays at the right edge, so lines cross the other panes to reach it.

blocks.quote: A captured box can be resized by dragging its edges and corners.
blocks.note: If a captured table got cut off, drag the box to fit it again.

blocks.quote: Drag the handle on the left to change the order of blocks.
blocks.note: Dragging a section moves the blocks under it too.

blocks.markdown: Memos can carry an **ID** and a title. Hover a memo to see + ID and + Title at the top right, or start the memo with something like `REQ-04 ` to turn it into an ID.

blocks.quote: Saved notes must still be there after the app restarts.
blocks.note: Write a note, restart the app and check. Note files live in `Notes/*.iwnote` (Korean Vaults use `노트`).

blocks.quote: Highlights must point to the same text after pages are reordered.
blocks.note: Reorder pages with Edit pages, then click this memo and check it lands on the same sentence.

blocks.quote: only writes a file that is actually smaller.
blocks.note: Compress only replaces the file when the result is smaller, so a PDF never grows.

blocks.quote: Cloud API keys are stored in this PC's credential store.
blocks.note: Enter a key once and it stays after a restart. Use local (Ollama) translation for sensitive documents.
